key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast long-term photoluminescence degradation of perovskites from early time-series data, generalizing across unseen materials.
engineering_relevance: This could shorten stability-testing cycles for perovskite solar materials by enabling earlier screening of promising compositions and degradation pathways.
method: Collected >86k photoluminescence spectra from 167 metal halide perovskite samples under heat and light stress.
Featurized spectra with a physics-informed model to capture interpretable stability descriptors.
Trained a hybrid CNN-LSTM to predict future PL intensity for unseen samples.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on diverse perovskite groups and outperformed baseline benchmarks while generalizing to samples not seen during training.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and coverage of the accelerated-aging dataset, so extrapolation to new stress conditions or chemistries should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
